solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ironing needing immediate attention

definitions.meaning: smoothing clothes with a hot iron

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both the household chore of flattening clothes and the sense of something urgent that cannot wait.

clue.text: Help relative, in a way

indicators.note: the relative is placed in the middle of the other pieces, so in signals insertion here

parts.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street, a way
a sister, shortened to sis, is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to help a family member in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts SIS inside A ST; 'in a way' reads as one phrase but splits into indicator, letter and abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid someone is a straightforward synonym for lending a hand to them.

clue.text: Uninteresting accommodation

definitions.meaning: a dull, lifeless performance can be called ...
an apartment, a home on one floor of a building

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dull or lifeless and an apartment, the British name for a self-contained home in a block.

clue.text: A pole manoeuvred round stern of hired boat

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the extra letter, which sits inside them
the letters of a pole are moved about into a new order, as a craft is manoeuvred
the stern is the back of a boat, so this takes the last letter of hired

explanation.surface: Someone steers a punt pole around the back of a rented boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvred' turns A POLE into PEALO, and 'round' puts D inside it. 'hired boat' reads as one phrase but 'hired' only supplies its stern.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal-powered pleasure craft hired at seaside resorts and boating lakes is a kind of small vessel.

clue.text: Reading about peak in Tanzania, might that be steep?

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of reading are rearranged
the peak of a word is its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone reading up on a Tanzanian mountain wonders whether its slopes are steep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges READING to GRADIEN; 'peak in' gives the top letter of Tanzania. Reading is not the English town here.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope's steepness is measured as its incline, so a steep one is a high incline.

clue.text: Come across a soft fruit

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for soft
a pear is a soft fruit

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles upon a ripe, squashy piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft fruit' looks like one description, but 'soft' gives P (piano) and 'fruit' gives PEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across as something is to seem or look that way, so the phrase means to seem.

clue.text: Responsibility ours?

definitions.meaning: a burden or duty that falls on someone
split as ..., something that is ... is ours to deal with

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: split the answer into ON US, and something that is on us is ours.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or duty is something on us, which makes it ours to carry; the second reading splits the word in two.

clue.text: Decide to tackle this puzzle again?

definitions.meaning: to make up one's mind firmly
split as ..., to work out the crossword a second time

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun on the prefix RE- (again) plus SOLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a firm decision is one sense; read as re-solve it means working out the crossword a second time.

clue.text: Mature writer on middle of trip

indicators.note: in an across answer the writer is put on, after, the other piece
the middle of a four-letter word is its two central letters

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An author matures during a trip, mid-journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' looks like an author but is the instrument; 'on' puts it after the middle of trip in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or cheese that matures grows ready for eating, the verb sense used here.

clue.text: Author, fleet of foot

explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift was the Irish satirist; the ordinary adjective means quick or fast-moving.

clue.text: Look at plaiting dreads with minimum of skill

indicators.note: plaiting weaves strands into a new pattern, so these letters are rearranged
the minimum part of the word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A hairdresser eyes some dreadlocks to be plaited, needing very little skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plaiting' rearranges DREADS to ADDRES; 'minimum of' gives the first letter of skill.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to look at it or deal with it, the verb sense.

clue.text: Barge in open site travelling round river

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the river letter
travelling suggests movement, so the letters of open site are moved about

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A canal barge travels round a river to an open site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges OPEN SITE to INTEPOSE and 'round' puts R inside. 'Barge' looks like a boat but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrupt a conversation uninvited is to intrude, putting oneself between the speakers.

clue.text: Team put in tenant's payment for occupant

indicators.note: the team is placed inside the other word

parts.note: a tenant pays rent to the landlord
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A team's money goes into the rent paid by whoever lives there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Team' reads as a crew of tenants, but a sports side is meant; 'put in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives in a place is its inhabitant or occupant.

clue.text: Whistler really experiencing freedom, first of all

indicators.note: first of all means the first letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistler' suggests the painter, but it is the match official who blows the whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee controls a football match by blowing a whistle, so is a whistler.

clue.text: Fine breaking piece of crockery for savage

indicators.note: breaking shatters the word fine, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a dish is an item of crockery

explanation.surface: A fine is imposed for breaking a dish, which seems savage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' looks as if it acts on the crockery but scrambles 'Fine' before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruel, wicked act is devilish or brutal, the adjective sense of savage.

clue.text: Joke that may backfire just the same?

definitions.text: Joke that may backfire just the same?

parts.words: Joke that may backfire just the same?
parts.note: a quip that, fired backwards, reads exactly as it does forwards: a three-letter palindrome

explanation.surface: A joke may backfire, ending the same as it started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfire' suggests a joke going wrong, but here it means reading backwards: the word is the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner told by a comedian is a quip or jest, and this one is a palindrome.

clue.text: Right in dirt, type of rock

indicators.note: the right letter is placed in the word for dirt

parts.note: gunge is British slang for sticky, messy dirt or goo

explanation.surface: Right in the dirt sits a kind of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' means music, not stone. GUNGE is British slang for sticky gunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seattle style of alternative music from the early 1990s, played by Nirvana, is a genre of rock.

clue.text: Diamond, perhaps? It is real, surprisingly, set around ring

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are set around the ring letter, as a stone is set
surprisingly suggests something unexpected, so the letters of it is real are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the diamond real? Surprisingly yes, set in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' turns IT IS REAL into SLITAIRE and 'set around' puts O inside. The surface is all jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A single gem set alone in a ring, often a diamond, is called by this name.

clue.text: Bigger beer round back of bar

indicators.note: the beer goes round the other letter

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A bigger beer is bought as a round at the back of the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a round of drinks but puts LAGER around R.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative form of large means greater in size.

clue.text: I live on Rhode Island and a European peninsula

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
RI is the US state abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A traveller claims to live in Rhode Island and in a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply joins the pieces in order here.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain and Portugal share the large south-western peninsula of Europe, named after the ancient Iberians.

clue.text: Arguably a kangaroo rat

definitions.meaning: a kangaroo moves by leaping, so could be called one that bounds
a rat is a cad, a dishonourable man

explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' is a cad, not the rodent, and 'kangaroo rat' is a red herring: a real hopping rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad or scoundrel is an old-fashioned insult; a leaping animal is one that bounds.

clue.text: Put up with huge beast

definitions.meaning: a large furry mammal such as a grizzly

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to tolerate; the noun is the large furry mammal such as a grizzly.

clue.text: Pip covers head of timid horse

indicators.note: the seed goes round and covers the other letter

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Pip, a character, covers the head of a timid horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pip' looks like a name but is a fruit seed; 'covers' puts SEED around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A mount for riding, especially in literary use, is a horse.

clue.text: Search for Indian on the radio?

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a Sikh is a follower of a religion founded in the Punjab, India

explanation.surface: Someone searches for an Indian station on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the radio' means the word is heard: SIKH sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To look for something is to hunt or search for it.

clue.text: Element damaging organ

indicators.note: damaging breaks up the word organ, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some element is harming a church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble gas found in air, atomic number 18, is a chemical element.

clue.text: Batters terribly idle, yes?

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters of idle yes are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer asks if lazy batsmen are terribly idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batters' looks like players at the crease but means things that bat, as one bats an eyelash.
explanation.definitionFit: One bats one's eye covers when blinking or flirting, so they are things that bat.
